html:
A battle fought on 3 September 1260 at the spring of Ain Jalut in the Jezreel Valley of Galilee. The Mamluks of Egypt defeated a Mongol army sent by Hulegu, founder of the Ilkhanate.

Two years earlier the Mongols had sacked Baghdad and ended the Abbasid caliphate. They then took Aleppo and Damascus. When news came that the Great Khan Möngke had died, Hulegu took most of his army back east, leaving a smaller force under his general Kitbuqa. The Mamluk sultan Qutuz marched north to meet it. His officer Baybars lured the Mongols into a trap with a feigned retreat, and Kitbuqa was killed.

It was the first major defeat of a Mongol army in open battle. The Mongols never held Syria or reached Egypt. Baybars soon killed Qutuz and took the throne, and the Mamluk state became the main power of the Arab world for 250 years.
